transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah… I came in because I can’t stop thinking I missed something with the cab, like even after I already did the safety check. I’ll know I checked it, but then while I’m driving it just hits me like, what if I missed something and somebody gets hurt, or my boss thinks I lied about checking it.

And it’s stupid because I try to tell myself I already did it, but it doesn’t shut up. Even when I’m trying to study, it pops back in. I mean, I’ve always been kind of careful with cars—my uncle used to say if you don’t listen to the engine you’re asking for trouble, and I guess that stuck with me—but this feels different. It just keeps going and I can’t focus.

When you have these thoughts about missing something with the cab, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly to try to ease the worry, like checking again, counting, or going over things in your mind?

Yeah, I do. Before I take a ride I’ll go around the cab checking everything—the tires, lights, doors, the meter, the paperwork. And then I’ll think, no, that didn’t feel right, or maybe I looked too fast, and I start the whole thing again.

Sometimes I take pictures too, like proof that I checked it, but then even the pictures don’t always help. It’s embarrassing because people are waiting, or I’m already late, and I’m still circling the car like… like I can’t just get in and go. My cousin jokes I inspect the car more than an airport security guy, which, I mean, would be funny if it wasn’t messing up my day.
How much do these thoughts and checking behaviors bother you, and have they affected your work, studies, or relationships with others?

It bothers me a lot. Like, it’s not just annoying anymore, it’s actually messing things up. I’ve lost rides because I couldn’t get on the road on time, and I’ve gotten warnings for it too, which makes me even more nervous.

And my studying… I’m supposed to be working on my CDL stuff, but then the day gets eaten up by checking or being late or trying to make up for it. I’ll sit down with the book and then realize I’m already behind on everything.

I don’t really see my friends much now either. They’ll ask me to come out, and I’m either still working because I fell behind, or I’m trying to catch up on studying. One of my friends keeps saying I’m acting like I’m 40 with three jobs, but it’s really just this checking stuff taking over.
Have you ever had these kinds of intrusive thoughts or checking behaviors before this recent period, or is this something that started more recently?

I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I’ve always been kind of careful, like with cars especially, because in my family people are always saying you don’t mess around with that stuff. My uncle would go on these long speeches about tires and oil and how one little thing can ruin your whole day, and I guess I listened.

But this kind of thing… the going back and back again, where I can’t just trust myself? I’m not sure. It feels more recent, but then I start thinking maybe I’ve always done little versions of it and didn’t notice. I don’t know if that makes sense. I guess it’s hard for me to tell where “being careful” stopped and this other thing started.

When you have these intrusive thoughts about missing something with the cab, do you feel driven to perform certain behaviors or mental acts to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah… I do feel like I have to. Like before I can take the ride, I’ll go around the cab checking the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, the paperwork… and then I’ll get this feeling like, wait, did I really check that tire or did I just look at it?

So I start again. Sometimes I take pictures too, like proof, but then even that turns into, “Was the angle right?” or “Maybe I missed something next to it.” It’s stupid because the passenger might be standing there, and I’m already late, but I still feel like if I don’t do it the right way, something bad could happen.

Do you ever have these kinds of intrusive thoughts or feel the need to check or do something to ease the anxiety in situations that aren’t related to the cab, like at home, school, or with other activities?

I don’t know… I mean, I haven’t really thought about it like that. Most of what I notice is with the cab, because that’s where it turns into a whole thing, you know?

At home or school, I’m not sure. Like, I’ll double-check stuff sometimes, but everybody does that, right? Like my mom will tell me to make sure the door’s locked, and then she’ll ask again five minutes later, so then I’m thinking, well maybe that’s just normal. My family’s always been kind of like that with safety stuff.

But the cab is the big one. That’s the one where I get stuck. Other places… I don’t know, I’d have to think about it more.

Can you think of any other situations—like at home, school, or during other activities—where you feel the need to check something repeatedly or have intrusive thoughts that won’t go away, even if they seem small or silly?

I mean… the cab is the main thing. That’s where I can really say it happens. Before I take a ride, I’ll keep going around the car, checking the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, the paperwork, all of it.

And it’s not just once. I’ll finish and then suddenly think, “Wait, did I actually check that?” So I start over. Sometimes I take pictures, which I know sounds like a lot, but then even the pictures don’t always help because I’ll think maybe I didn’t get the right angle or I missed something.

Like, my uncle used to always say cars are unforgiving, one small thing and then you’re stuck on the side of the road or worse, and I guess that kind of sticks in my head. But yeah… even if a passenger is waiting and I’m already late, I still feel like I have to do the whole check again if it doesn’t feel right.
Outside of checking the cab, do you ever find yourself stuck on thoughts that won’t go away or feel like you have to do something a certain way to ease your mind, even if it seems small or silly?

Yeah… I mean, outside the cab, it’s more like the thought follows me around, if that makes sense. Like I’ll know I did the safety check, I can remember doing it, but then this thing hits me like, what if you missed something, what if a tire was wrong or the paperwork wasn’t right, and then somebody gets hurt.

And then I’m driving and I’m trying to act normal, because obviously you can’t be sitting there freaking out with someone in the back seat asking about traffic or whatever. People always want to talk about the weirdest stuff in taxis, too, like one guy was telling me about his divorce the whole ride and I’m just nodding, but in my head I’m stuck on, did I lie when I said the cab was okay?

It happens when I’m trying to study too. I’ll be looking at school stuff and suddenly I’m back to thinking my boss is gonna say I lied or I skipped something. I can’t really make it shut up. It’s like even when I know I checked, my brain doesn’t accept it.

Have you ever had unwanted or intrusive thoughts about things like contamination, harming someone, needing things to feel 'just right,' or other disturbing ideas that you can't seem to get out of your head, even if they don't happen as often as with the cab?

Not really like contamination or “just right,” I don’t think. It’s more the cab thing that gets stuck in my head.

Like, I came in because even when I know I did the safety check, the thought still hits me that I missed something and then somebody could get hurt, or my boss is gonna say I lied about checking it. And it doesn’t just stay at the car, it’ll be there while I’m driving or even when I’m trying to study.

Sorry, I know I keep coming back to that, but that’s the one I can’t really make shut up.
